messages.subject: questions around hierarchical ordered logit
parts:
Hi All,

I have been trying to build a hierarchical ordered logit (below), and am hoping for feedback. This is in the framework for MRP (multi-level modeling and post-stratification to adjust for non-response bias in convenient samples), so I am trying to put out the linear predictor per row in my population-level data set. Please ignore the empty loops in the model, they stem from a script automating the model itself (I hope it does not unduly influence stan).

#1) does the model look fine to you?
#2) For confidence intervals, I currently compute three dimensional arrays and assess uncertainty from there by simulating N_pops(100)*N_category distributions over all responses.  

 
holder<-array(NA, c(X[['N_pops']],data_structure$responses$n_levels,100))
  for (p in 1:data_structure$responses$n_levels){
    if (p==1)
    {holder[,p,]<-(1/(1+exp(params[["eta"]][,w,]-params[[paste0("c_",data_structure$responses$response_name)]][,p])))}
    else if (p>1 & p<data_structure$responses$n_levels)
    {holder[,p,]<-(1/(1+exp(params[["eta"]][,w,]-params[[paste0("c_",data_structure$responses$response_name)]][,p])))-
      (1/(1+exp(params[["eta"]][,w,]-params[[paste0("c_",data_structure$responses$response_name)]][,p-1])))}
    else {holder[,p,]<-(1 - (1/(1+exp( params[["eta"]][,w,]- params[[paste0("c_",data_structure$responses$response_name)]][,p-1] ))))}
  }

for( j in 1:data_structure$responses$n_level){
        y.pred[,j] <- sapply(1:100, function(x) sum( input_data$pops_N * holder[,j,][,x] ) / sum( input_data$pops_N ))
      }

I then awkwardly assess confidence by 
for( j in 1:data_structure$responses$n_level){
        y.pred[,j] <- sapply(1:100, function(x) sum( input_data$pops_N * holder[,j,][,x] ) / sum( input_data$pops_N ))
      }
      #adjust cis
      pred_temp_national<-rbind(apply(y.pred,2,quantile,prob=0.025), y.pred[which.max(params$lp__),],apply(y.pred,2,quantile,prob=0.975))
 

Is there a better way? I really have a hard time of thinking about this in a >2 choice setting.

#3) I would like to make credible intervals comparable to margin of error (currently, uncertainty bands in my model are much wider). Is it fair to scale somewhere by sqrt(N) or something akin?

Many thanks,
Tobi

We don't have good prior recommendations for these as far as I know. I think global cut points are more common than varying ones, but we're big fans of hierarchical modeling, so if you can figure it out, that'd be great. I didn't see any hierarchical structure in your model or a prior for c_vote.

Empty loops won't do anything---the C++ compiler is usually good enough to ignore all this.

For standard errors on the posterior means, we divide the posterior standard deviation by the sqrt of the number of effective samples. It's all estimated.

- Bob

I also realized we did say something on our priors page. I should look
at our own Wiki:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Prior-Choice-Recommendations


• Prior for cutpoints in ordered logit or probit regression
• For full Bayes, uniform priors typically should be ok, I think.
• For modal estimation, put in some pseudodata in each category to prevent "cutpoint collapse."
• Cutpoints are ordered (by definition). Put the prior on the differences between the cutpoints rather than the cutpoints themselves.
• Alternatively, put a prior on the cutpoints and partially pool them, not to a constant, but to a linear function. That is, if the cutpoints are c[1],...,c[K], don't do c[k] ~ normal(mu, sigma); instead do c[k] ~ normal(a + b*k, sigma), estimating the hyperparameters a and b from data. It will probably make sense to put informative priors on a, b, and sigma too.

- Bob

beta_stat_education[education[i]]+

vectorizing ordered_logistic yet.

transformed data {
real scale_const;
real scale_dyn;

scale_dyn =0.05;
scale_const =5;
}

can be just

transformed data {
real scale_const = 5;
real scale_dyn = 0.05;
}

Hi Bob,

Thanks for the comment, and a very late apologies for the code. It stems from a text-parsing script, hence the odd spacing etc. but I should have checked before submitting! 

I am still not getting a hierarchical ordered logit to converge. Again, the model is roughly modeled after page 143 in stan reference 2.14 and gelman/hill 2007, chapter 13. Then, we draw class of outcome from an ordered logit where the combination of group-specific random effects is the linear predictor, and every group has a separate ordered vector of cutpoints. I tried a number of fixes ("break" meaning bad convergence, as in R Hat):

- change the order of hierarchies: draw a global vector of random effects (i.e. a length-4 vector for 4 age-brackets , and then draw a group-specific vector of random effects from a multivariate normal 
- let the model try to estimate off-diagonals of the correlation matrix of the multivariate priors (breaks)
- run simple models with one class of random effects only (breaks)
- run as Bernoulli to avoid "cut-point collapse" (breaks)

I must be missing something obvious here! The cleaned up model is attached (I am not concerned about the efficiency of the loop right now). 

Any thoughts?

Thanks again,
Tobi
